title: The North Wind and the Approach of God
english: "Will they take the wickedness from you, or will they flee in these things?" Having rebuked her who, the divine word seeing, had done an abomination in his house, the Lord calls her name an olive tree of easy access; your branches have become useless. For how have the branches that fell through their own unfaithfulness become useless, especially having moved into the storm of life, in which there are billows and a multitude of salty and bitter waters.

Regarding the unfaithful branches having come to the sea and being torn apart by a very strong wind, it is said concerning this ruined city—the Jewish one, I say—and by another prophet, who is Micah, by God: "I will scatter the stones of it into chaos and I will uncover its foundations" (Micah).

When these gloomy things have come upon the wretched synagogue of the Jews, it is necessary for us, those having believed in the Savior, to become a fruitful olive in the house of God and toward the rising in the mount of olives, so that we may also be transferred into the divine paradise by the grace of God, becoming imitators of Christ, concerning whom it is written: "Behold, a man, rising is his name" (Zechariah 14:4).

"Half of the mountain shall lean toward the north and half of it toward the south. And the gorge of my mountains shall be blocked, and the gorge of my mountains shall be joined up as far as Asher, just as it was blocked in the days of the earthquake in the days of King Uzziah of Judah" (Zechariah 14:4-5).
The half, he says, of the mountain—clearly the mount of olives—will lean toward the north, toward the one deviating into the sea and the chaos, the other half reaching toward the south.

What are the north and the south? From the Breath of Breaths, the Church having been ravished by her own bridegroom, is to learn, saying: "Arise, north, and come, south, blow upon my garden and let my aromas flow."

The north in these things is the evil power, rather Satan himself; the south, being the Savior himself, is approached as the bridegroom. Therefore, when the very cold north is present, the flow of the divine aromas is hindered, the pores being choked because they become thickened due to the coldness of the north and become hard; the bride flees from this and calls to the south, so that by his warmth [she may...]

From the sources of the intelligible, the fragrances flow, concerning which it is said toward the bridal chamber of the spiritual spouse: 'The fragrance of your myrrh is above all spices' (Song of Solomon 1:3). The north wind is said to have heat and to be an invigorating breath, having learned that fire exists and came to cast upon the earth, as he himself announced saying: 'I came to cast fire upon the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled' (Luke 12:49).

It must be said: 'Arise, north wind,' not by voice alone but in reality, so that it may be sent from afar. In deeds, he says: 'Arise, north wind,' to the faithful soul saying to the teacher who speaks: 'Turn away from evil and do good,' and to the Apostle who wrote to the whole Church: 'Test all things, hold fast to the good. Abstain from every kind of evil' (1 Thessalonians 5:21-22). The north wind, driving the abstention from every kind of evil and the turning away from evil, urges the south wind to come so as to draw near to it through pious faith and moral virtue. For thus, to those being thus prepared, the provider of all good things comes, as the theologian James wrote: 'Draw near to God and He will draw near to you' (James 4:8).

Having the longing for His presence, and being near to: 'Come, south wind,' in that bridal drama he hints: 'Come, my sister, let us go out to the field' (Song of Solomon 2:10). This is equivalent to: 'Arise, north wind, and come, south wind,' and to: 'Draw near to God and He will draw near to you, resist the devil and he will flee from you' (James 4:7-8), as the one resisting the devil says to him: 'Arise, north wind,' and the one drawing near to God entreating the south wind to come to him, the God Logos, concerning whom in the song of the prophet Habakkuk, according to some interpreters, it is brought forth instead of: 'God will come from Thaman,' [as] 'God will come from the south wind,' the coming of the Father from the south wind of the bride, according to that which is said by Him in the Gospel: 'He who receives me receives him who sent me' (John 13:20). For in whatever way he who sees Him sees the Father, so the one receiving Him receives the Father abiding in Him, in whom is His Only-begotten.

What will happen when turning toward the north and the south of the clarified mountain of olives, or when the gorge of the mountains of God is blocked and is joined even unto Asahel? The gorge and the joining could not be understood otherwise than by having known what the mountains of God are.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Earthquake in the Days of Josiah
english: Regarding his mountains, the prophets have said in accordance with the subject that there is a height belonging to them not only of knowledge and wisdom, but also of the application of practical life. For concerning these things, the hymn-singer spoke toward the origin of all: 'You shine wondrously from eternal mountains' (Ps 103:2). For how could they not be eternal mountains, from which God wondrously illuminates the knowledge of the truth and broadly the knowledge concerning the Trinity, those who gaze upon unseeing eternal things according to the apostolic exhortation (2 Cor 4:18)?

The abyss of the depth of the obscurity of those things spoken in enigma is a gorge of these mountains, which he who came to fulfill the law and the prophets (Matt 5:17) has unblocked, having leveled with his own teaching and presence the rough and uneven ground of those things spoken with concealment, so that it might appear easy to traverse through smoothness. This having happened, the gorge of the mountains was joined to the text through the appearing of harmony, up to Asaph, who was called 'deaf to the feet' because of the speed of his walking, according to the sharp-seeing gaze; for this animal is perceptive, as the appellation itself shows from the word 'gazing'. Therefore, up to Asaph, the attachment of the mountains shall be, being known to the perceptive.

In the same way, the obstruction of the mountains has occurred as in the days of the earthquake, which existed in the days of Uzziah, the king of Judah. We have not found a perceptible earthquake having occurred at all while Uzziah was reigning, neither in the Kingdoms nor in the Chronicles; therefore, what is written about him must be understood allegorically. And see lest a shaking occurred during Uzziah, intending to seize the priesthood for himself. For having entered into the temple of God, and having approached the holy altar, he attempts to offer sacrifice through himself and not through the priests (2 Chron 26:16). The daily priest, most boldly asserting this transgression, while coinciding with the others, saying: 'It is not yours, Uzziah, to burn incense to the Lord, but that of the priests,' he was distressed, and he stretched out his hand with anger to be seized by the guards to harm them; but immediately his hand was struck, as if to cast the tyrant out of the temple instantly, having been struck by the holy [place] as far as the porch, because of his insolence.

[...] having taken a practice not fitting for another except for the priests presiding in the temple. 5.62 Regarding the encounter with that which it is determined to draw to itself, the works of the kingdom were hindered by the unclean leprosy, while he was performing them, the rest of his son who was about to receive the rule. 5.63 In the days of the earthquake from the commingling, a precipice became attached to the mountains, in the days of Judah, while Ozias was reigning. 5.64 The earthquake now being declared lies also at the beginning of the prophet Amos: 'For words,' says Amos, 'which came from Tekoa, two years before the earthquake in the days of Ozias,' the earthquake being said here, according to the circulating Jewish tradition, of the vision appearing to Isaiah, concerning which it has been written thus: 'It happened in the year in which King Ozias died, I saw the Lord sitting upon a high and lifted-up throne, and Seraphim were standing around him, six wings to the one and six wings to the other' (Isa 6:1-2), and after a little: 'And the other cried to the other: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Sabaoth, full is the heaven and the earth of his glory' (Isa 6:3).

5.65 Full is the heaven and the earth of the glory of God became, after the death of Ozias with which he practiced lawlessness. For how could there not be a shaking of change toward the better having happened by the seeing of God, so that the heaven and the earth might be filled with his glory, and a removal might occur of the lawlessness of the one discovered in seeing the divine vision, and a remission of the sins of all the people? 5.66 In the days of the death of Ozias, who desired to plunge the divine laws, desiring to seize for himself the priestly service not fitting to him, there was attached that which he had newly cut through by a cleavage of the laws, so that the priest might again unhinderedly perform his own things in the temple, and the king, attending to the protection of those in authority, was no longer touching the priestly things because the care of the holy things was not to be held by him. 5.67 Or is Asael here a name of a place; let him be heard by the one having circled the places of Judah, having grasped something that seems accurate. 5.68 And the Lord my God shall come, and all the saints with him. In that day there shall not be light. And there shall be frost and ice one day (Zech 14:5-7).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Eternal Day of the Lord
english: And that day is known to the Lord. And it shall not be day nor night, and towards evening there shall be light.

The present voice is able to signify a second and glorious appearance of the Savior, concerning which John in Revelation spoke highly and God-appropriately thus: 'Behold, he comes with the clouds, and every eye shall see him, and those who pierced him' (Rev 1:7). This understanding is based on what the Savior said concerning himself: 'Clouds shall see the Son of Man coming upon the clouds of heaven with much power and glory' (Matt 24:30). For how could he who comes royally not shine with much glory? And he comes also with much power, with the saints coming with him, not of men alone but also of angels. For it follows that 'those having become his attendants and servants' and 'the ministering spirits having been sent for service' shall shine with him, so that he himself may be known as their king and they as his powers, that is, an army.

On the day in which the Lord God shall come, there shall not be perceptible light, because of the true and eternal light making him [bright], according to what was pre-proclaimed in Isaiah concerning the perfect illumination, having it here: 'The sun shall not be your light by day, nor the rising of the moon shall light your night, but the Lord shall be to you an eternal light, and your God shall be your glory' (Isa 60:19-20). It must also be said thus: those not possessing light need that which shines upon them, not needing this when they themselves have become light.

Since therefore in the future age, called allegorically 'day', 'the righteous shall shine like the sun in the kingdom of their own Father', having been made light and shining themselves, they pass through the day not needing an external light. And indeed in this life, having enlightened themselves with the light of knowledge as having heard from the Savior: 'You are the light of the world' (Matt 5:14), they pass through in a bright state not from another, but from light of themselves and of a day being present, concerning which the choir of the saints sings: 'Let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us' (Ps 33:3). Toward this spiritual Jerusalem having much holiness, the prophet says, being seized by God and having the Holy Spirit: 'Be enlightened...'

“Shine, Jerusalem, for your light has come upon you, and the glory of your God has risen upon you. Behold, darkness and gloom will cover the earth upon the nations; but upon you the Lord will appear, and the glory of your God will rise upon you. And kings will go to your light, and nations to your brightness” (Isa 60:1-3).

How is it not that it exists bright and illuminated, since this is being announced—the light having come to be from having been illuminated, as if divine brightness were being revealed? Understand, if possible, how so to impose upon the coming prophetic voice.

When the Lord Pantokrator comes with His saints, the state of those being judged will be such that each one who is ignorant of his own [deeds] will not have light, so as to need “the one illuminating the secrets of darkness and revealing the purposes of hearts” (Heb 4:13), so that, “having been revealed before the judgment seat of Christ” (2 Cor 5:10), they may receive what is worthy of what they did through the body, both good and evil.

And since there will be confusion and turmoil for those being judged, being gathered together and being tossed about, on a single day there will happen heat and ice to the souls of men, in the expectation of those being liberated from the gloomy and the oppressive, as the Gospel proclaims.

The day of the Lord, being continuous and not being interrupted by a night intervening, will be known to God, “since the existing light has no darkness at all” (Rev 22:5), and for this reason, being neither day nor night, but the day being eternal, the sun no longer making the day, nor the moon illuminating the night, according to the prophet, as it was said nearby, the Lord being eternal light. Even if ever indeed some should enjoy the day, toward evening there will be light, as God illuminates all things.

This day, being thus understood and occurring, will be known to the Lord, being worthy of His knowledge, according to what is signified and written: “The Lord knew those who were His” (2 Tim 2:19). This voice does not contradict the Gospel voice which says: “Concerning that hour and that day no one knew, nor the angels, nor the Son, but the Father alone” (Matt 24:36).
